newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends up on foreign fund inflows.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends up on foreign fund inflows.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed slightly higher against its U.S. counterpart on Friday as foreign funds continued to flow in for the bullish stock market, dealers said.
The local dollar ended at T$27.507, off an intraday high of T$27.491, against Thursday's T$27.522 close.
Turnover through dealers was a heavy US$341 million.
Dealers also attributed the higher close to reflect the weakness of the greenback overseas.
"But overall, the Taiwan dollar is pretty stable, consolidating around the T$27.50 level," said one dealer.
The Taiwan stock index, which has surged more than 1,200 points or some 18 percent in 1997 alone, gained 1.01 percent on Friday on frenzied turnover of T$149.717 billion to close at 8,162.68 points.
But dealers noted importers' persistent U.S. dollar demand when the local dollar neared T$27.50, which offset the Taiwan dollar's appreciation.
A T$27.49-27.53 range was seen for Saturday.
